discovery: Chiral effective field theory of nuclear forces, founding a systematic, improvable theory of atomic nuclei rooted in QCD

nominees.name: Ubirajara van Kolck
nominees.affiliation: IJCLab (CNRS/Université Paris-Saclay), France, and University of Arizona, USA

motivation: For decades nuclear forces were phenomenological potentials with no clear link to QCD and no way to estimate their errors. Building on Weinberg's proposal, van Kolck carried out the first consistent derivation of nucleon-nucleon and three-nucleon forces from chiral symmetry, establishing power counting and showing why many-body forces are hierarchically suppressed. Epelbaum and Machleidt turned this framework into precise, high-order interactions (up to N4LO and beyond) that describe scattering data with the quality of the best phenomenological models. Chiral effective field theory now underpins ab initio calculations of nuclei from the lightest systems to lead-208, neutron skins, drip lines and neutron-star matter. Because each order is systematically improvable, it lets theory give predictions with quantified uncertainties that can be tested against experiments on exotic nuclei. It has turned nuclear structure from model-building into a predictive science grounded in the Standard Model.
